requirements.title: Relabel an item that awaits a finished package
requirements.rationale: An item that points at a package that is done will never be closed by anyone.

criteria.condition: a package has landed and an open issue labelled `af:awaits` carries an `af:awaits-<NN>` whose package is finished or is no package under the spec root or its archive
criteria.action: remove `af:awaits` and `af:awaits-<NN>` from the issue, add `af:defect` and `af:severity-correctness`, and comment on it
criteria.contract: after the step the issue carries `af:defect`, `af:severity-correctness` and its `af:from-<MM>`, and neither awaits label; one comment names the rule `awaits-finished`, the package it awaited and the commit of the base branch

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/labels_test.go, beside the label-check tests, a table over open issues after package 02 landed, with 01 archived, 02 just landed, 03 open and no package 09: {af:awaits + af:awaits-02 -> defect; af:awaits + af:awaits-01 -> defect; af:awaits + af:awaits-09 -> defect; af:awaits + af:awaits-03 -> no write; a closed issue with af:awaits-02 -> no write; af:defect with a stray af:awaits-02 and no af:awaits -> no write}: assert the labels afterwards and that each comment contains 'awaits-finished', the package id and rev-parse(main)

criteria.condition: a package has landed and every open `af:awaits` issue names a package with a task still pending or in progress
criteria.action: leave the issues as they are
criteria.contract: the forge records no write for them

criteria.action: for any issue the rule has already relabelled, change nothing when the rule runs again
criteria.contract: a second run records no forge write

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/labels_test.go: apply the rule twice to the table of REQ-1.1: assert the second application records no AddLabels, RemoveLabel or AddComment call

requirements.title: Stop before building on a serious defect
requirements.rationale: A later package silently builds on a lost write or a leaked secret.

criteria.condition: a package has landed and, after the label rules, an open issue labelled `af:defect` and `af:from-<NN>` carries a severity in `--stop-on`, which is `security,data-loss` when the flag is absent
criteria.action: stop the loop and start no further session
criteria.contract: exit code 1; `result.stopped.reason` is `serious defect` and `result.stopped.issues` lists each such issue with its number, URL, title and severity; the package's ledger line has outcome `landed` and holds the same issues

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/stop_test.go (new), a table over the open issues the fake session leaves for 01 and the flag: {defect data-loss, default -> stop; defect security, default -> stop; defect correctness, default -> go on; defect minor, default -> go on; defect correctness, --stop-on correctness -> stop; untested, default -> go on; deviation, default -> go on; defect data-loss labelled af:from-00, default -> go on; a closed defect data-loss -> go on; an item relabelled to a correctness defect by awaits-finished, default -> go on}: assert the exit code, result.stopped.issues and whether 02's session started

criteria.condition: `specrun` is started and the last package that landed still has an open defect of a severity in `--stop-on`
criteria.contract: exit code 1 with the same `result.stopped` as REQ-2.1; no session starts; once the issue is closed, loses the severity, or `--stop-on` no longer holds it, the next start goes on

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/stop_test.go: after a stop on a data-loss defect of 01: run again -> exit code 1 and no session; then a table of what the person does {close the issue; replace af:severity-data-loss by af:severity-minor; pass --stop-on security}: run again -> 02's session starts

criteria.action: take the severities to stop on from it, a comma-separated list of `security`, `data-loss`, `correctness` and `minor`, the empty string meaning never stop, with `SPECRUN_STOP_ON` as its default when set
criteria.contract: a value outside the four is a usage error with exit code 2 that names it and lists the four; with `--stop-on ''` a package with an open security defect does not stop the loop

check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/flags_test.go, beside the existing flag tables: {absent -> [security, data-loss]; 'minor' -> [minor]; 'security,correctness' -> both; '' -> []; SPECRUN_STOP_ON=minor with no flag -> [minor]; 'severe' -> exit code 2 naming 'severe'; 'security,' -> exit code 2}

requirements.title: Show in a dry run what the label rules would change
requirements.rationale: A person should see what an unattended command will do to their issues before it does it.

criteria.condition: `--dry-run` is given and a forge client can be made
criteria.action: report every change the label rules would make as the labels now stand, and whether the stop rule would fire, and write nothing to the forge
criteria.contract: `result.would_change` lists each change with the issue's number, the rule (`incomplete-labels`, `awaits-finished`), the labels it would add and remove; `result.would_stop` lists the issues the stop rule would name; both are `[]` when there are none; the forge records no write

setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
check.pseudocode: in internal/specrun/labels_test.go: with one unlabelled issue of the last landed package, one af:awaits issue toward a finished package and one open data-loss defect of the last landed package: run --dry-run; assert result.would_change has two entries with the rules and labels of the contract; assert numbers(result.would_stop) == [the defect]; assert the in-memory forge recorded no write and no session started

execution_paths.title: A package lands on a data-loss defect and specrun does not start the next one

steps.action: starts the session for the first package
lands the package, files one data-loss defect and leaves one item awaiting a package that landed long ago
checks the landing and the labels, and relabels the awaiting item as a correctness defect with a comment
lists the package's open defects, finds the data-loss one, writes the ledger line and stops with exit code 1, naming the issue
closes the issue after fixing the defect and runs `specrun` again
finds no serious defect left for the last landed package and starts the session for the second package
